_purpose: Canonical loaded terms scanned deterministically in the article's OWN VOICE and injected as bias-extractor candidates alongside the model's extraction passes. This closes the closed-vocabulary half of a coverage gap three prompt generations could not close (D1 held at ~3.3 across live/v2/v3; the `regime` canary was found 1 time in 5 by v3 while a string scan finds 5 of 5). The open-ended half — evaluative framing, emotionalizing, quote handling — stays with the LLM. Deterministic-before-LLM, applied to the half that is a vocabulary rather than a judgement.
_contract: Every entry is EVIDENCE-SOURCED: `note` names where the term was already cited — the live extractor prompt, RUBRIC-bias_extractor.md, or a specific judge finding in one of the three breadth evals. No entry is invented. Matching is case-insensitive on word boundaries; multi-word terms are allowed. A hit is a CANDIDATE, not a finding: the downstream bias judge clears figure-backed descriptors, attributed language and defensible word choices, so this list may over-generate within that tolerance by design.
_language_note: English only. Articles reaching this stage are English (the writer emits English); per-language lexicons are a separate task.
_not_covered: `passive_obscuring` is a grammatical construction, not a vocabulary — a term list cannot find 'the fees were raised' in general. Only the one idiom the prompt and rubric both cite is listed. That pattern stays the model's job.
